       We also attempted to replicate the well-established associative-priming effect using a
visual lexical decision task (e.g., de Groot, 1984, 1987; Neely, 1967, 1977). This task was
included to confirm the reliability of our experimental procedure, such as the statistical
methodology and the seriousness of the participants. The task and the stimuli were provided by

required participants to categorize letter strings as words or nonwords. Each stimulus (target
word) was preceded by a prime word that is either a semantic associate of the target (e.g., dog
– cat) or is unrelated to the target (e.g., uncle – cat). The dependent variable of interest was the
decisions.reason: Beek explicitly empirically retests associative priming in H6; serving as a reliability check does not exclude replication. The complete recovered Matzke2015 and associated same-report priming document establish an empirical related/unrelated RT finding, so its earlier one-URL access gap is obsolete. Beek nevertheless attributes the task/materials to Matzke and the well-established finding to a grouped e.g. citation of deGroot1984/1987 and Neely1967/1977, without selecting which source-specific empirical component is retested. A supplier that also reports an effect is not automatically the selected original; conversely, changed tasks or absence of every original manipulation do not by themselves exclude conceptual retesting. All shipped/corrected rows cover Ackerman mental-state claims, so no priming target is falsely declared represented. The original1984 full body remains unrecovered after recorded attempts; the available primary description distinguishes proportion/SOA/neutral-baseline components but does not resolve which selected component or closest report Beek empirically targets. Allocation between this grouped antecedent and the directly adopted Matzke task/report remains genuinely ambiguous, not a verdict that priming was untested. Participant-level overlap and exact current OSF timing are unverified, but universal cohort nonoverlap is not required and is not the reason for withholding. No original data are accessed, no source is invented, and all prior contrary opinions/spent calls remain preserved.
